newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge up in thin trade, focus on U.S..
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge up in thin trade, focus on U.S..

text.p: Irish bonds edged slightly up in thin late trade on Tuesday as the market looked to the U.S. for direction, dealers said.
Dealers said the market awaited the release of U.S. November producer prices data on Wednesday to be followed by November consumer prices figures on Thursday.
"These figures could tell us a lot about the state of the U.S. economy in terms of inflation," one dealer said.
"The feeling is that the next move in terms of U.S. interest rates will be an upward one," the dealer added.
By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained five pence to 101.75 to yield 5.98 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 edged up five pence to 108.90 to yield 6.60 percent.
Dealers said they saw no independent impulse in the Irish market as international bonds markets continued to consolidate their positions after heavy losses late last week.
Analysts forecast a 0.3 percent rise in U.S. November producer prices, compared to a rise of 0.4 in October, while a rise of 3.0 percent year-on-year is expected.
Consumer prices are expected to be up 0.3 percent in November and 3.0 percent year-on-year.
